What the Care Team Has Already Told You

Instructions, contacts and follow-ups for your husband's care in one place.

Download PDF

The nurse's instructions are on a sheet in your bag, the planner's number is on a card somewhere, and your son said he'd call someone about something.

Nothing on this page needs explaining or deciding. It's an inventory: what you've been given, where it is, what date is on it and who has it.

What to collectWhere it isDate on itWho has it
The date the arrangement changes, and who told you
Written instructions from the care team for after the change
Anything you were told out loud and wrote down yourself
Any instructions about how he moves around, or about falls
Any instructions about when someone should be with him
His medication list: prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins and supplements
Any instructions about the place he's going
Who to call with questions, including nights and weekends
The name and number of the discharge planner, social worker or care coordinator
His doctor's office and his pharmacy, with phone numbers
Appointments or visits already scheduled

Follow-ups someone has already promised

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Any row above with empty boxes. Put a name beside each one.

For example Nothing in writing about nights. I'll ask the planner on Thursday.

How to use it

  • Copy the date from the paper itself. If a sheet has none, note that and ask whoever gave it to you for a dated copy.
  • For something said out loud, write who said it and on what day. Keep their wording.
  • Leave the instructions themselves where they are. This page only says where to find them.
  • Keep the page with the papers, and take both to your next conversation with the care team.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what an instruction means or whether it still applies. If two papers seem to say different things, or one of them is unclear, that's a question for the people who wrote them.

Where this comes from

The rows for written instructions, the medication list and who to call follow what Medicare's discharge checklist tells patients and caregivers to ask for and keep. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's working list for this step.
